toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: I collected two items. X2 (independent surveyor reports) covers the whole stoppage from a neutral source. X14 (tamper-proof RFI audit trail) tests the claim's second pillar directly. I skipped the others, because the main conclusions were already settled and further items would mainly bear on the incentive link.
output.brief:
Ruth — the slip was mainly Callerby's own doing, and the drafted claim should not go to Halden.

The lender's independent surveyor (reports copied to both sides; Callerby replied 'no comments') recorded that the level 3–4 steel was on site and erection was due to start on 21 October. The tower crane was taken to another Callerby job on 20–22 October; no frame work followed until it returned in April, and erection restarted within days. Change order CO-09 wasn't issued until 6 November: four beams on one level, fitted in a week with a hired crane. The other changes were interior work with spare time. The tamper-proof RFI platform shows the architect answered 62 of 64 requests on time; the 'late' count came from Callerby's own drafts sitting unsent for up to 47 days. I'm about 90% sure.

Next: pull the claim; take legal advice and settle with Halden, resisting only its extra-cost demands. Don't discipline the superintendent — he told the truth. Review how the crane decision and the November 'design hold' report came about, and require sign-off before plant or crews move between projects. Hold off suspending the Kestrel incentive: nothing yet shows it drove the decision.
